title: Sea warmth gave no clear common link to local catch concentration in four US trawl samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether seasonal sea warmth was linked to more concentrated catch weight within trawl hauls. We used public OceanAdapt catches from Eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US Fall in 1982-2019, with fixed strata and area weights. Four region and period models controlled linear year. Only late Bering had a clear positive main slope: 1.19 concentration points per C, with a four-test interval of 0.53 to 1.85. The other three intervals included zero. Removal of pollock kept a smaller positive late Bering link. Equal stratum weights and consecutive annual differences gave intervals that included zero. Thus, a common clear positive response did not repeat. Catchability, surface temperature, short series and survey changes limit inference. This is a catch association, not a causal climate effect. We do not measure pollution or ecological timing. Code, cleaned catch evidence, climate evidence, source hashes, all checks and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Local catch concentration and seasonal temperature slopes in two regions and two periods. Main intervals use a four-test correction and linear year control. One concentration point is 0.01 index units.
